newsitem.title: INDIA: India call ends off day's high, seen in same range.
newsitem.headline: India call ends off day's high, seen in same range.

text.p: Indian call money ended Friday easier and dealers said they expected rates to remain around 10 percent next week.
Call money ended the day in the 10.25-10.50 percent range after touching an intra-day high of 11.25 percent in early trade, dealers said.

Dealers said call money rates were likely to remain at Friday's closing levels over the next week as some liquidity was likely to be drained away from the banking system due to a forthcoming auction of government securities.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said it would auction 20 billion rupees of five-year securities on November 26.

"Even though the auction falls outside the current reporting fortnight, sentiment will be affected," said a dealer at a foreign bank. Banks report their positions to the RBI on November 23 when the current fortnight draws to a close.
"There also seems to be no factors in the coming days which will improve liquidity from current levels," the dealer said.

Dealers said they expected a yield of around eight percent at the five-billion rupee weekly auction of 91-day treasury bills to be held later on Friday. The yield at last week's auction was 7.23 percent.

"With call money rates moving up, yields will have to rise," said a dealer. "We expect market participation to be less than the notified amount and some amount is likely to devolve on the RBI and primary dealers."
Dealers said prices of government securities fell before recovering in light trade on Friday.

The 13.50 percent 1997 government of India stock fell to 102.30 rupees from Thursday's 102.40 before recovering to 102.60. The 14 percent 2005 stock slipped to 102.45 rupees from 102.49 before strengthening to 102.55.
Dealers said prices rose on purchases by provident funds.
"These funds are looking for long-dated securities as it suits their funds flows," said a dealer. "At current rates, investments are quite attractive."

Dealers said commercial paper maturing in February was traded in the secondary market at a yield of 11.5 percent. Paper wtih January maturity was traded between 11.25 percent and 11.50 percent, they said.
No trades were reported in certificates of deposit.
